shared_elements: schematic incised signs/motifs in registers or rows
justification: Both surfaces bear shallow schematic carvings including circular/curvilinear motifs and some figural elements, but A is a flat wall covered with dense horizontal rows of small repeated script-like signs plus a small figure and boat-like shape, while B is a three-dimensional block-like anthropomorphic statue whose torso and head carry a few large isolated motifs (a ring/disc on the back, paired curved arcs, band-like elements). The organisation—continuous registers of tiny repeated signs versus a handful of oversized emblems distributed over a body form—differs fundamentally, and the shared traits (incised circles, schematic rendering) are the kind any carving tradition could produce independently.
